items.title: Divergent nitrous oxide accounting can distort crop carbon intensity scores and agricultural trade
items.abstract: Methods for estimating nitrous oxide emissions, a major contributor to the carbon intensity of nitrogen fertilizer-dependent crops, can produce substantially different results across frameworks. Standardized approaches are needed to avoid distorting trade and strengthen incentives for mitigation of emissions.

items.title: Wheat resilience under compound stress
items.abstract: Compound hot–dry–windy events are becoming more frequent and increasingly damaging to wheat yields in China’s wheat belt, underscoring the need for improved crop management, breeding and climate adaptation.

items.title: Wheat yield sensitivity to compound hot–dry–windy events is increasing in China
items.abstract: Increasing hot–dry–windy events threaten wheat yields in China, with significant yield losses linked to high-temperature, low-humidity conditions. Analysis of extensive yield and climate data reveals worsening sensitivity trends, emphasizing the need for adaptive strategies in agricultural practices.

items.title: When conflict with industrial fishing threatens coastal communities
items.abstract: We developed a global index to identify small-scale fishing communities that are most vulnerable to conflict with industrial fleets. Areas with highest vulnerability, where fishing supports many livelihoods and essential needs, were found to be concentrated in Africa and Asia. Our results highlight priorities for equitable fisheries governance.

items.title: Selective extraction of phenolic compounds from barley waste using deep eutectic solvents
items.abstract: In this study, the development of an ultrasound method for extraction of phenolic compounds from barley waste using acidic deep eutectic solvents (UAE-DES) was investigated. Optimization of the extraction parameters, which include extraction time, temperature, and ultrasound power (UP), was performed using the One-Factor-at-a-Time (OFAT) experimental design, followed by HPLC-PDA for determination of total quantified phenolic content (TQPC). In addition, the influence of water addition on TQPC was evaluated. The Maximum TQPC obtained was 5.78 mg/g using ChCl: formic acid at a molar ratio (1:2) and optimal conditions of (70 °C, 30 min, 80% UP, 10% water), and 4.67 mg/g, using ChCl: tartaric acid at a molar ratio (1:2) and optimal conditions of (70 °C, 25 min, 100% UP, and 20% water). The obtained TQPC was 5- and 4-fold higher in comparison with 70% methanol and 70% ethanol extraction. LC–MS-qTOF analysis of DES extracts revealed diverse phenolic compounds, while the concentration range of compounds obtained was as follows: ferulic acid (0.86–2.47 mg/g), catechin (0.12–2.16 mg/g), p-coumaric acid (0.12–0.32 mg/g), naringenin (0.54–0.86 mg/g), and apigenin (0.15–0.91 mg/g). SEM analysis confirmed enhanced accessibility of lignocellulose in DES-treated samples. The sustainability of UAE-DES extraction was assessed using AGREE, AGREEprep, CACI, BAGI, and CaFRI green tools. The grade assessment of each tool resulted in scores: 0.63 for AGREE, 0.57 for AGREEprep, 65 for CACI, 82.5 for BAGI, and 72 for CaFRI, indicating a greener extraction performance of UAE-DES in comparison with …

items.title: The assessment of gastric myoelectrical activity between different stomach regions based on three-channel electrogastrogram signals: a pilot study
items.abstract: IntroductionPrevious studies have widely used surface electrogastrogram (EGG) signals to non-invasively evaluate gastric motility. However, it focused only on the assessment of electrical activity in a certain stomach region and lacked the analysis of interactions between different gastric regions. In the study, we aimed to assess the correlations of myoelectrical activity between distinct stomach areas using functional connectivity (FC) methods by three-channel EGG for the first time.MethodsThe study contained 20 healthy subjects and the dataset for each subject consisted of two three-channel EGG signals (labeled as CH1, CH2 and CH3; CH1 projected onto the region of lesser curvature, CH3 projected onto the region of greater curvature, and CH2 positioned the region between CH1 and CH3) with a sampling rate of 2 Hz acquired from three locations of stomach during a 20-minute period of fasting and postprandial states respectively. Firstly, the EGG signals were band-pass filtered into three slow wave (SW) bands by finite impulse response (FIR) filter, namely bradygastria (0.017-0.033 Hz), normogastria (0.033-0.067 Hz) and tachygastria (0.067-0.15 Hz). Secondly, we employed four FC algorithms (i.e. Spearman correlation coefficient (SCC), phase lag index (PLI), mutual information (MI) and coherence (Coh)) to calculate the connection strength of each pair of gastric areas. Finally, the FC strength between fasting and postprandial conditions for all subjects or the normal weight (NW) or overweight (OW) people and between the NW and OW groups for both fasting and postprandial states…

items.title: Quality evaluation of a traditional Chinese medicine compound preparation containing Rhodiola rosea, Astragalus membranaceus, and Carthamus tinctorius
items.abstract: ObjectiveWe aim to improve the quality control of Rhodiola rosea, Astragalus membranaceus, and Carthamus tinctorius capsules (RAC capsule) from the aspects of thin-layer chromatography (TLC) and high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC), respectively, and the established quality control methods are suitable for their popularization and application in large-scale production.MethodsA TLC method was established for the identification of R. rosea, A. membranaceus, and C. tinctorius in RAC capsules. A HPLC method with gradient elution and UV detection was established for simultaneous determination of salidroside, tyrosol, hydroxysafflor yellow A (HSYA), anhydrosafflor yellow B (ASYB), and rhodiolin.ResultsThe TLC chromatograms showed distinct and reproducible spots for the RAC capsule samples at positions consistent with those of the corresponding reference crude drugs, while no interfering spots were observed in the negative control samples. The HPLC method demonstrated excellent linearity (R2 > 0.9991) for all five analytes within their respective concentration ranges with precision, stability, and repeatability; RSDs all below 2%; and average recoveries ranging from 95.07% to 105.61%.ConclusionThe developed TLC and HPLC methods are specific, accurate, and robust, providing a reliable quality control strategy for RAC capsules. The study supports the standardization of this herbal capsule formulation and establishes a foundation for further pharmacological research and clinical investigations.

items.title: Complementary techniques for investigating the molecular dynamics of uncrystallized water
items.abstract: Uncrystallized water (UCW) refers to the fraction of water in hydrated materials that remains uncrystallized upon cooling. Rather than forming bulk ice, this water retains molecular mobility even below the nominal freezing point. In polymers and proteins, UCW includes strongly bound water associated with specific functional groups and more weakly confined water residing in nanoscale environments. As a result, it plays an important role in mechanical behavior, structural stability, and biological function. Because UCW is heterogeneous, no single technique can fully capture its properties, and multiple complementary methods are required. This review highlights how dielectric spectroscopy (DS), nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR), differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), neutron scattering, particularly quasielastic neutron scattering (QENS), and terahertz and infrared spectroscopies each probe different aspects of UCW across distinct time and different sample sizes. We outline what each technique measures, the models commonly used to interpret the data, and how combining these approaches helps distinguish between “free,” “bound,” and “non-freezable” water. Studies that apply multiple methods to the same samples, with consistent control of hydration and temperature, are essential for developing a coherent and quantitative picture of UCW. This integrated approach is also key to translating UCW behavior into practical design principles for cryopreservation, pharmaceutical freezing, and biomaterials. Importantly, complementarity arises from differences in timescale and the distinct …

items.title: Kefir-fermented camel milk: physicochemical characteristics, sensory evaluation, and consumer behavior in Morocco
items.abstract: Althou⁠g⁠h camel milk is gen⁠erally acknowledged for its nutr⁠itional content and medicinal effects, the processing technolo⁠gy and consumer acceptability of its fermented products rem⁠ain⁠ to b⁠e improved. This study aimed to ev⁠alua⁠te Moroccan consu⁠mers’ perception of and intention to consume camel milk fermented with kefir grai⁠ns and investigate the effect of enrichment with natural date extract on the physicochemical and sensory characteristics of the product. A survey was conducted with 1,009 participants from different regions of Morocco to study consumption habits, knowledge of fermented c⁠amel milk products, and the intention to consume kefir-fermented camel milk. In parallel, camel milk formulations fermented with kefir gra⁠ins, unflavored, f⁠lavored with sucrose, and enriched with date extra⁠ct we⁠r⁠e developed and characteri⁠zed through physicochemical analyses, sensory acceptance, and preference tests. Both flavored⁠ formulations were standardized to the same soluble solids content (8.13 °Brix), ensuring comparable s⁠weetness during physicochemical and⁠ sensory evalua⁠tion. The results indicated that information on nutrition⁠al benefits positively influenced consumption intention. Enrichment with date extract significantly modified the physicochemical characteristics and improved sensory ac⁠ceptability compared with that of the sucrose-flavored formulation. These findings indicate that da⁠te extract can be used to modify the p⁠hysicochemical characteristics and improve the sensory accep⁠tance of camel milk kefir while contribu⁠ting to the valorization of loca…

items.title: Assessment of probiotic characteristics of lactic acid bacteria isolated from traditional foods of Southern India for preparation of sauerkraut
items.abstract: Probiotics are highly essential for a healthy gut in order to maintain optimum microbial balance, fight against pathogenic bacteria, improve digestion and maintain overall intestinal health. The present investigation was carried out to evaluate the probiotic properties of lactic acid bacteria (LAB) isolated from traditional fermented foods of Southern India. The isolates cultures were tested for acid production using titratable acidity, and six maximum acid-producing (g/L) isolates (DFRM9 11.0, DFRM8 10.0, DFRA9 10.0, DFRD4 10.0, DFRY4 8.0 and DFRD11 7.0) were selected for further analysis. Acid tolerance, bile tolerance, tolerance to the gastrointestinal tract, antibacterial activity, and antibiotic susceptibility, were tested on the above LAB isolates and isolates obtained earlier such as Bifidobacterium bifidum NCDC229, Lactiplantibacillus plantarum DFR4, Pediococcusacidilactici DFR1 obtained during previous studies in our laboratory. Analysis of variance (ANOVA) indicated that Limosilactobacillus fermentum DFRM9 had significantly (p < 0.05) higher probiotic effects among the tested isolates. L.fermentum DFRM9 was used as a starting culture for sauerkraut preparation, and its fermentation activity was compared with that of spontaneous fermentation. The developed functional food was found to have desirable physico-chemical and microbial quality. The results obtained in the present investigation support the use of lacto-fermentation for the production of sauerkraut and indicate the potential of lactic acid bacteria isolated from traditional foods as probiotics in various p…

items.title: Highly sensitive detection of soybean-derived DNA in soy sauce using an integrated PCR-CRISPR/Cas12a nucleic acid detection platform
items.abstract: IntroductionSoy sauce is a traditional fermented condiment with widespread global consumption, and its authenticity depends on the requisite use of soybeans as a primary ingredient. However, for economic gain, soybean has been partially or completely substituted with cheaper materials, including other legumes such as pea or peanut, or non‐soybean nitrogen sources such as acid‐hydrolysed animal protein derived from feathers or hair. Such practices constitute economic fraud and labelling violations and may introduce undeclared allergens, raising legitimate concerns regarding food safety and consumer trust. Conventional DNA‐based detection techniques are often hindered by DNA fragmentation and the presence of PCR inhibitors in the complex, fermented matrix, leading to compromised sensitivity and reliability.MethodsTo overcome these limitations, we developed a novel nucleic acid detection platform that synergistically combines target pre‐amplification via polymerase chain reaction (PCR) with highly specific sequence recognition and signal amplification utilizing the CRISPR/Cas12a system.ResultsThis integrated approach achieved a detection limit of 10 femtomolar (fM) for a synthetic Le1 target DNA standard, which compares favourably with many existing methods. The practical applicability of this assay was preliminarily evaluated on 22 commercially available soy sauce samples from various markets.Discussion This study establishes a sensitive and reproducible endpoint‐fluorescence tool for the detection of soybean‐derived DNA. The assay holds promise for routine food authenticatio…

items.title: Effect of pumpkin pulp (Cucurbita maxima) pigments as natural colorants in ice cream: extraction efficiency, bioactive compounds and sensory acceptance
items.abstract: IntroductionPumpkin (Cucurbita maxima) pulp is a promising source of natural pigments with potential applications as food colorants. This study evaluated three extraction methods and the sensory acceptance of pumpkin-derived pigments in ice cream.MethodsMaceration, Soxhlet extraction, and supercritical CO2 extraction were compared in terms of extraction yield, total carotenoid and flavonoid contents, and DPPH antioxidant activity expressed as IC50. Analytical determinations were performed in triplicate. Extraction methods were compared using one-way ANOVA followed by Tukey’s HSD test. The Soxhlet extract was selected for ice cream formulation, which was evaluated by 100 untrained adult panelists using a five-point hedonic scale. Sensory data were analyzed using the Kruskal–Wallis test followed by Dunn–Bonferroni comparisons.ResultsSupercritical CO2 extraction resulted in the highest carotenoid content (315.22 ± 0.01 mg kg−1) and total flavonoid content (1099.08 ± 0.04 mg QE kg−1 extract). Soxhlet extraction achieved the highest extraction yield (22.72 ± 0.33%) and the lowest IC50 value (1.06 ± 0.035 mg/mL). The formulation containing 600 mg of extract per 600 g of ice cream (Z3) showed the highest color acceptance. Significant differences were detected for color (p < 0.05), but not for odor, flavor, or texture (p > 0.05).DiscussionThe extraction method affected both extraction yield and the measured characteristics of the pumpkin extracts. The results support the potential of pumpkin-derived pigments as natural food colorants, although further work is needed to evaluate the…

items.title: A new spin on catalysts: A roadmap for smarter chemical reactions
items.abstract: Electron spin is a quantum property that makes electrons behave like tiny magnets. It can influence how electrons interact with each other and how chemical reactions take place. But what does this have to do with producing fertilizers, making cleaner fuels or improving energy technologies? What connects all these processes is the use of catalysts, materials that help chemical reactions happen faster and more efficiently. By controlling electron spin, scientists may be able to improve how these catalysts work, opening up new possibilities for more efficient chemical processes.

items.title: Asymmetric atomic structure improves sodium–sulfur battery performance
items.abstract: Chinese researchers have developed a new way to improve sodium–sulfur battery performance by changing the atomic structure of a catalyst. Led by professors Wang Hui and Zheng Fangcai from the High Magnetic Field Laboratory at the Hefei Institutes of Physical Science of the Chinese Academy of Sciences, the study is published in Angewandte Chemie.

items.title: More power, less payoff: Study reveals a bottleneck in cleaner methanol production
items.abstract: Dialing up the power on electricity-driven chemical reactions doesn't guarantee that they'll be more efficient, suggests a new study, a finding that gets researchers closer to creating the ideal conditions for sustainable chemical manufacturing.

items.title: Molecular dinitrogen anions pave the way for low-temperature ammonia synthesis
items.abstract: While ammonia (NH₃) is best known for its role in fertilizer production, it is attracting attention as a carbon-free hydrogen carrier, potentially offering a practical way to store and transport clean fuel. Despite this promise, NH₃ synthesis still depends on high-temperature, high-pressure processes that are difficult to scale up sustainably. The reason behind this is the extremely strong bond between nitrogen atoms in nitrogen gas (N₂), which requires a lot of energy to break.

items.title: Scientists discover a plastic-eating “Pac-Man” enzyme with a surprising secret
items.abstract: Scientists have discovered a remarkable “Pac-Man enzyme” that helps bacteria devour certain types of plastic and may offer new hope in the fight against plastic pollution. Researchers found that several biodegradable plastics completely broke down in soil within about a year, while conventional plastic remained largely unchanged.

items.title: Scientists discover why a 100-year-old mushroom disease won't go away
items.abstract: Scientists have uncovered a surprising secret behind a mushroom disease that has frustrated growers for more than a century: It involves more than 17 species of harmful bacteria, not just one. The discovery could explain why treatments have struggled to stop the disease and open the door to more effective, eco-friendly solutions.

items.title: The “glue” holding your cells together has a surprising second job
items.abstract: Scientists have discovered that E-cadherin, a protein best known as the “glue” holding cells and tissues together, has a surprising second job: helping epithelial cells swallow nearby dead cells. Using live zebrafish and mouse embryos, researchers found that cells can dramatically reshape their lower surfaces to engulf cellular debris while keeping their upper surfaces stable, allowing protective barriers to remain sealed.

items.title: Scientists find evidence for two origins of life on Earth
items.abstract: Scientists probing life’s deepest origins have uncovered evidence that the first free-living cells may have emerged not once, but twice. The findings suggest a striking possibility: life may share one ancient genetic code, yet have undergone two separate transitions into free-living existence.

items.title: AI helps Stanford scientists discover a “natural Ozempic” with a surprising advantage
items.abstract: Stanford researchers have discovered an AI-identified natural molecule that dramatically suppresses appetite and promotes fat loss in animals, potentially offering an Ozempic-like weight-loss treatment without common digestive side effects or significant muscle loss. Called BRP, the molecule reduced food intake by up to 50% and targets a different brain pathway, raising hopes for a more precise obesity treatment if future human trials prove successful.

items.title: Scientists discover new Alzheimer’s drug that repairs DNA damage and reduces brain inflammation
items.abstract: Scientists have discovered that a drug originally developed for spinal cord injuries can tackle several key features of Alzheimer’s disease, including DNA damage and inflammation. Already tested for initial safety in humans, the experimental treatment could offer a faster path toward therapies that target the disease at its roots.

items.title: Experts say high blood pressure guidelines are missing half the equation
items.abstract: Scientists are calling for a major rethink of how we manage high blood pressure, suggesting that eating more potassium could be just as important as cutting back on salt. A new report finds that combining increased potassium intake with reduced sodium consumption may offer greater benefits for blood pressure control than sodium reduction alone.

items.title: Kids who eat more ultra-processed foods show a troubling brain response
items.abstract: A new study suggests that ultra-processed foods may influence children's developing brains in ways that encourage weight gain. Researchers from USC studied 46 children ages 7 to 10 and found that those who ate more ultra-processed foods showed stronger activity in the brain's reward system when viewing tempting foods like cookies and French fries. These heightened brain responses were linked to greater increases in body fat and body mass index (BMI) one year later, suggesting that the brain's sensitivity to food cues may help explain why ultra-processed diets are associated with obesity.

items.title: Influence of solvent extraction on phenolic profile using (HPLC–PDA), antioxidant activity, and nutritional values of Grewia tenax (Forssk.) Fiori fruits
items.abstract: BackgroundGrewia tenax (Forssk.) Fiori is a wild fruit traditionally consumed in arid regions and recognized for its potential nutritional and therapeutic value. This study compares the phenolic composition and antioxidant properties of G. tenax fruit extracts obtained using methanol, ethanol, and water to evaluate their benefits to human nutrition.MethodologyWhole fruits were extracted with the three solvents, and phenolic acids and antioxidant activities were analyzed using standard in vitro assays, including 2,2-diphenyl-1-picrylhydrazyl (DPPH), reducing power, and β-carotene bleaching tests. The total phenolic content (TPC) of the G. tenax fruit extracts was determined colorimetrically using the Folin–Ciocalteu method, while free phenolic acids were analyzed by HPLC-PDA. DPPH free radical scavenging activity was assessed by taking 3 mL of sample solutions and mixing different concentrates with each. New stocks of radical solutions were prepared every day. The reduction in absorbance of the resulting solution was observed for 10 min at 515 nm with a spectrophotometer.ResultsMethanol extracts contained the highest total phenolic content and six distinct phenolic acids, similar to ethanol, while water contained two. Gallic acid was dominant at 917.5, 136.5, and 188.2 μg/g in methanol, ethanol, and water extracts, respectively. DPPH scavenging activity followed the order L-ascorbic acid (89.01) > methanol (59.11) > ethanol (55.07) > water (52.14). Reducing power values were 2.79, 2.11, and 1.77, respectively, and β-carotene assays were positive for all extracts but lower th…

items.title: Ketogenic diet induces systemic and tissue-specific metabolic remodeling in mice: an untargeted GC-MS metabolomics study
items.abstract: ObjectiveTo systematically characterize the effects of a ketogenic diet (KD) on the serum and multi-tissue metabolomes of mice using untargeted gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS), with particular emphasis on systemic and tissue-specific metabolic remodeling.Methods30 specific-pathogen-free male C57BL/6J mice aged 5–6 weeks were randomly assigned to a ketogenic-diet group (KD, n = 15) or a standard-diet group (Std, n = 15) and maintained on the assigned diets for 28 days. Serum, heart, liver, spleen, lung, kidney, small intestine, hippocampus, skeletal muscle, and brown adipose tissue were collected for untargeted GC-MS metabolomic profiling. Principal component analysis, partial least squares discriminant analysis, differential-metabolite screening, and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes pathway enrichment and topology analyses were performed.ResultsThe metabolic profiles of serum and multiple tissues showed clear separation between the KD and Std groups. A total of 52 candidate differential metabolites identified using a nominal P < 0.05 threshold were identified, including 3-hydroxybutyrate, O-phosphoethanolamine, amino acids, fatty acids, and intermediates of the tricarboxylic acid cycle. Enrichment analysis indicated that KD primarily affected glycerolipid and glycerophospholipid metabolism, sphingolipid metabolism, fatty acid metabolism, the tricarboxylic acid cycle, pyruvate metabolism, amino acid metabolism, glutathione metabolism, and pyrimidine metabolism. The magnitude and pattern of these changes differed substantially among tissues.ConclusionA 28-…

items.title: Development and external validation of a nomogram incorporating the TyG index and prognostic nutritional index for predicting cardiovascular events in patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and chronic kidney disease
items.abstract: BackgroundHeart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) frequently coexists with chronic kidney disease (CKD), representing a high-risk cardiorenal phenotype within the cardiovascular–kidney–metabolic (CKM) syndrome. Despite the high burden of adverse cardiovascular events in this population, dedicated risk prediction tools remain limited. We aimed to develop and validate a prediction model for major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), defined in this study as the composite of all-cause death and first hospitalization for worsening heart failure, in patients with HFpEF and CKD by integrating biomarkers reflecting metabolic and nutritional-inflammatory status.MethodsThis retrospective cohort study included a development cohort of 2,363 consecutive patients with HFpEF and CKD between January 2012 and December 2023. The development cohort was randomly divided into a training cohort (70%) and an internal validation cohort (30%). An independent cohort of 713 patients from Wenzhou TCM Hospital of Zhejiang Chinese Medical University was used for external validation. Predictor selection was performed using Cox proportional hazards regression, and a nomogram was constructed based on the final multivariable model. Model performance was evaluated using time-dependent receiver operating characteristic curves, calibration plots, decision curve analysis, and Shapley additive explanations (SHAP).ResultsDuring a median follow-up of 1.41 years, 1,085 patients (45.9%) experienced MACE. The final multivariable model retained age, atrial fibrillation, ACEI/ARB/ARNI therapy, serum cr…

items.title: Fruit and vegetable consumption and obesity among adults in Saudi Arabia: a cross-sectional study
items.abstract: BackgroundObesity is a critical public health concern in the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) region (Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Bahrain and Oman), with Saudi Arabia having among the highest prevalence rates globally (23% adults obese, 45% overweight). These rates contribute to 27% of non-communicable disease (NCD) mortality and to an estimated US $19.3 billion in combined annual direct medical and productivity costs. Despite national targets to reduce obesity under Vision 2030, only about one in ten Saudi adults meets the recommended five daily servings of fruits and vegetables. Evidence on the relationship between fruit and vegetable consumption and obesity in this population remains limited.ObjectiveTo examine the association between fruit and vegetable consumption and body mass index (BMI) category among adults in Saudi Arabia, and to identify demographic factors associated with consumption patterns.MethodsAn exploratory cross-sectional study was conducted between December 2022 and (May 2023) using an online Food Frequency Questionnaire (FFQ) distributed via social media platforms to a non-probability convenience sample. The study included 641 adult participants (≥18 years) residing in Saudi Arabia. BMI was calculated from self-reported height and weight and classified into WHO BMI categories. Consumption frequencies were summed into monthly consumption frequency scores. Statistical analysis included descriptive statistics, Kruskal-Wallis and Mann–Whitney U tests, multiple linear regression, and multinomial logistic regression with BMI category…
items.authors: Ayman Mohammed Almekhlefy, Sadeq B. Abu-Dawas, Maha Khalid AlYousef et al.

items.title: Continuing Medical (Anatomy) Education Series: Organ Donation and Transplantation, a Means of Continuity of Functional and Independent Life and Living
items.abstract: Diseases and disease processes are key components of life and living. The understanding and appreciation of this axiom will impact greatly on the quality and standard of human health and life. The human body is bedeviled by a myriad of diverse and large spectrum of pathologies. These vary from hereditary, infectious, inflammatory, metabolic, structural degradation, genetic alterations, neoplastic, toxicological injury, ageing and trauma. All these reduce the functionalities of the affected organ/ organ system. There are established first line management strategies for these pathologies, however more often than not, they may not suffice. At this stage, the replacement of such organ becomes the only option for optimal quality of life or continuity of life. This can only be achieved through tissue and organ donation and transplantation. Over the decades, steady advancements are being made in the medical field of human tissue and organ donation and transplantation. Thus it becomes pertinent for students of human medicine to be well and adequately educated on the issues that relate to the donations of human tissues and organs and their transplantation. Such issues covered in this article include global statistics on organ donation and transplantation; historical antecedents of organ donation and transplantation; sources of organ transplants; tissue transplants; set guidelines and standards by The World Health Organization, The European Parliamentary Research Services and The Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare Nigeria.

items.title: Effect of Quinoa Protein Concentrate in Particulate and Fibrillar Forms on the Physico-Chemical Properties of Quinoa Starch Gels
items.abstract: The current study investigates the interactions between quinoa protein—both in particulate (protein concentrate, QPC) and fibrillar (QPF) forms—and quinoa starch (QS) gels, and how these interactions influence the thermal, pasting, and rheological properties of the gels. Gels were made by adding three different concentrations of QPC or QPF to a 10% QS dispersion (10, 25, and 50% w/w of starch). DSC results suggested an enhancement of amylopectin thermal stability and an acceleration of retrogradation upon a cooling stage by the addition of quinoa protein. FTIR spectra indicated that QS and QPC/QPF mostly interacted through hydrogen bonds. According to rheological measurements, in contrast to the increased G′ due to the addition of QPC (50%), only a slight increase in G′ was observed due to the addition of QPF (50%). Notably, this study is the first to directly compare the effects of QPC and QPF on starch gel properties, revealing that QPC markedly enhances gel elasticity. These findings highlight the potential application of the optimized quinoa starch-protein-based gels as functional ingredients in plant-based meat analogues, where improved textural and nutritional attributes are critical.

items.title: Relationships Between Chemical Compounds and Sensory Properties of Virgin Olive Oil in the US and Israel: Development of a Prediction Model for Defects
items.abstract: Virgin olive oil (VOO) quality is defined by both chemical and sensory parameters. While the chemical parameters are objective and measured using instrument-based methods, sensory quality evaluation is based upon human panels, which can be subjective, have less repeatability, suffer from fatigue, and require long and costly training. Tasting biases could be minimized by a trained panel, but using humans as a testing instrument is inevitably prone to various psychological biases, stimulus-related factors, and carry-over effects. The objectives of this study were to evaluate instrumental methodologies that will assist the existing human panel in assessing the sensory characteristics of VOO and to develop chemistry-based predicting models for sensory properties in the oil using VOO samples originating from the US and Israel. Our results indicated that oil rancidity highly correlated with the contents of chemical components contents; 1-penten-3-one, 3-hexen-1-ol, (E)-2-pentanal, and 1-octen-3-ol are the major volatiles associated with rancidity defects (low concentrations of these compounds). Positive sensory attributes, such as fruitiness, correlated with 1- acetoxypinoresinol and hexanal, while bitterness correlated with pinoresinol, the aldehydic form of oleuropein aglycones, and the dialdehydic form of oleuropein aglycone. The random forest model suggested that luteolin, (E)-2-hexenal, 1-penten-3-one, and C18:0 are the most useful measurements in predicting the occurrence of sensory defects in the olive oil samples included. items.title: Synergistic effects of biochar and poultry manure on soil and cucumber (Cucumis sativus) performance: A case study from the southeastern Nigeria
items.abstract: This study explores the suitability of different biomass feedstocks for biochar production and their effects on soil health and crop yield. Two planting seasons were conducted, involving cucumber as the test crop and eleven treatments combining biochar and poultry manure. Soil analysis revealed initial soil conditions with high sand content and low pH. Poultry manure and biochar exhibited pH, organic carbon, and nutrient level variations. Significant differences in cucumber growth and yield were observed, with the longest vine length in plots treated with palm kernel husk biochar and poultry manure. Residual effects in the second planting season displayed similar trends. Soil pH, organic carbon, and total nitrogen remained consistent between seasons, while available phosphorus increased significantly in plots amended with goat manure biochar and poultry manure. Calcium, magnesium, potassium, and sodium contents also varied. Fruit length, weight, and yield were significantly improved by biochar treatments, with the combination of palm kernel husk biochar and poultry manure yielding the highest fruit weight. Correlation and structural equation analyses (p < 0.05) highlighted the relationships between plant characteristics, soil properties, and fruit indices, emphasizing the importance of nitrogen and phosphorus in supporting fruit development. The study suggests that biochar application enhances soil nutrients, crop growth, and fruit yields while reducing reliance on chemical fertilizers. items.title: Adsorptive Removal of Volatile Organic Compounds from Industrial Effluent Using Synthesized ZnO-CA Composite Base Adsorbent
items.abstract: In this study, a composite adsorbent consisting of ZnO nanoparticles and cellulose acetate nanoparticles was prepared. The composite was extensively characterized through Scanning electron microscopy (SEM), Transmission Electron Microscopy (TEM), Energy Dispersive X-ray Spectroscopy (EDX), and Brunnaeur Emmet Teller analysis (BET). Batch adsorption experiments were carried out to study the effects of concentration of adsorbate (10- 80 mL), dose of adsorbent (0.1 – 1 g), pH(3-13), contact or exposure time (30-180 minutes) and temperature(30 - 70℃) on the removal of benzene and toluene using the synthesized adsorbent. The pseudo-second-order model well described the kinetics of adsorption studied, and Langmuir's isotherm best described the isotherm modeling of the adsorption data. Thermodynamic studies revealed that all the adsorption processes are feasible, endothermic, and spontaneous. The prepared adsorbent is suitable for removing benzene and toluene from wastewater.

items.title: Production of L-lysine under submerged fermentation by Corynebacterium glutamicum using different agricultural plants leaves
items.abstract:
Introduction: This study investigated the production of L-lysine using Corynebacterium glutamicum and various leaf extracts (cassava, palm tree, maize, cowpea, cocoyam, and plantain). The study also explored the activities of amylases and proteases, as well as the levels of total soluble proteins, reducing sugars, glucose, flavonoid and phenolic contents, and pH changes. 
Materials and Methods: Different treatments (extract, boiled extract, extract + C. glutamicum, boiled extract + C. glutamicum) were examined for their effects on L-lysine concentration. Additionally, the activities of amylases and proteases, as well as levels of total soluble proteins, reducing sugars, glucose, flavonoid and phenolic contents, and pH changes, were analyzed. 
Results: Maize leaf extract + C. glutamicum exhibited the highest L-lysine concentration (1.771a±0.1 mg/g), while boiled cassava leaf extract showed the lowest concentration (0.023b±0.1 mg/g). Palm tree leaf extract had significantly higher reducing sugar levels compared to other extracts. Boiled plantain leaf extract fermented by C. glutamicum had the highest total soluble protein level (9.5±0.2 mg/g), while cassava leaf extract had the lowest (2.1±1.2 mg/g). 
Conclusion: Submerged fermentation of leaf extracts using C. glutamicum can be utilized for L-lysine production. The study highlights the influence of different leaf extracts and treatments on L-lysine production, as well as on amylase and protease activities, total soluble protein levels, reducing sugars, glucose, flavonoid and phenolic contents, and pH values. items.title: Renal protective effects of natural honey on animal model of hypertension
items.abstract: Hypertension, also known as high blood pressure, is a leading cause of cardiovascular disease and premature death worldwide. Numerous investigations have established that hypertension can cause alterations in the cardiovascular system as well as renal structure and function. Fresh honey is consumed worldwide and is claimed to be highly medicinal and has therapeutic effects against a wide range of medical conditions. We investigated the renal protective effect of natural honey in in animal model of hypertension. Forty (40) male albino rats, with average weight (120 ±10 g) were administered with high salt diet, HSD (80 g NaCl + 1 kg of diet and 1% NaCl in drinking water (10 g of NaCl + 1 L distilled water) for 10 weeks to induce hypertension in the rats. Following confirmation, hypertensive male rats were randomly selected for the experiment. Twenty (20) albino rats (15 hypertensive rats and 5 normotensive rats) were divided into 4 groups, Groups A-D. Group A: (Normotensive Control) no administration was given; Groups B-D (hypertensive rats) received the following treatments. Group B was treated with natural honey (15 ml/kg), Group C treated with hydrochlorothiazide (0.15 mg/kg), daily for 21 days; while Group D received no treatment, until the end of the 21 days administrations. Blood samples were taken in the end, and renal alterations were assessed via biochemical and histopathological analyses. items.title: The immune‐supportive diet in allergy management: A narrative review and proposal
items.abstract: The role of nutrition is increasingly recognized in the management of chronic immune diseases. However, the role of an immune‐supportive diet as adjuvant therapy in the management of allergic disease has not been similarly explored. This review assesses the existing evidence for a relationship between nutrition, immune function, and allergic disease from a clinical perspective. In addition, the authors propose an immune‐supportive diet to enhance dietary interventions and complementing other therapeutic options for allergic disease from early life to adulthood. A narrative review of the literature was conducted, to determine the evidence of the relationship between nutrition and immune function, overall health, epithelial barrier function, and gut microbiome, particularly in relation to allergy. Studies on food supplements were excluded. The evidence was assessed and utilized to develop a sustainable immune‐supportive diet to complement other therapies in allergic disease. The proposed diet consists of a highly diverse range of fresh, whole, and minimally processed plant‐based and fermented foods supplemented with moderate amounts of nuts, omega‐3‐rich foods and animal‐based products in proportional amounts of the EAT‐Lancet diet, such as (fatty) fish, (fermented) milk products which may be full‐fat and eggs, lean meat or poultry, which may be free‐range or organic.

items.title: Quality and Flavor of ‘Aliza’ Fruit: A Unique Pomelo × Mandarin Hybrid
items.abstract: ‘Aliza’ is a new pomelo × mandarin hybrid (Citrus maxima, cv. Red Chandler × Citrus reticulata, cv. Ora) developed by the Israeli citrus breeding program at the Volcani Institute. Here, we aimed to characterize the quality and flavor of ‘Aliza’ fruit as compared to other commercial citrus fruit, specifically pomelo (C. maxima), grapefruit (Citrus paradisi), orange (Citrus sinensis) and mandarin (C. reticulata). ‘Aliza’ fruits have a similar size as grapefruits, but have a thinner peel and a unique yellowish/golden color. ‘Aliza’ fruits are completely seedless and have especially high juice contents. They also have a unique, highly preferred flavor, characterized by high sweetness and moderate bitterness and acidity, with strong citrusy and tropical fruity aromas. Sensory analyses conducted with the aid of a trained panel and an electronic tongue revealed that the flavor of ‘Aliza’ fruits is different from the flavors of other citrus species. Consumer acceptance and preference tests revealed that ‘Aliza’ fruit are highly appreciated and favored. The aroma volatile profile of ‘Aliza’ fruit was somewhat similar to those of pomelo and grapefruit, but very different from those of orange and mandarin. Overall, ‘Aliza’ fruits can be distinguished from other citrus fruits by their unique color, high juice content and exceptional, unique flavor.

items.title: Flavor release and stability comparison between nano and conventional emulsion as influenced by saliva
items.abstract: Flavour release and emulsion stability depend on volatile organic compounds' environmental conditions, food microstructure, and physicochemical properties. The effect of pH (3.5 vs 7.0) and saliva addition on stability and flavour release from nano and conventional emulsions was investigated using particle size, charge and Lumisizer measurments. Larger particle sizes were observed at lower pressures and in saliva-containing emulsions. At 1700 bar, nano-emulsions (below 150 nm) were created at pH 3.5 and 7.0 including saliva-containing emulsions. As was clear from the creaming velocity measurements, saliva addition decreased the emulsion stability by reducing particle charges and increased viscosity by more than 50%, especially when prepared at pH 3.5 closer to the isoelectric point of the used emulsifier β-lactoglobulin (pH 5.2). (5.2). Flavour release from emulsions was measured at equilibrium using a phase ratio variation to determine partition coefficients and dynamically using an electronic nose. Partition coefficients of the flavour compounds for most conditions were two to four times lower in emulsions prepared at pH 7.0 than at pH 3.5 and in emulsions without saliva. Emulsions prepared with higher pressures showed stronger flavor release rates, while additional salvia dropped the release rate for ethyl acetate at pH 3.5. The physicochemical properties of flavour compounds, saliva addition and pH of emulsions influenced flavour release more than homogenization pressures.
